The goal of this notebook is to extract the large dams of the obstacles to
river flow referential (ROE), and to assess their impact on fish species
individually, then on food web structure along the river continuum (D11).
Large dams are obstacles with a drop height of at least 5 m; the >= 10 m
class is shown in the selection only. From the impact on species onwards,
all large dams (>= 5 m) are used, to have more dam data.

## Setup

```{r}
library(renv)
renv::load()
library(targets)
library(here)
tar_config_set(
  store = here::here("_targets")
)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
devtools::load_all()
nice_theme()
```

## Obstacles to river flow (ROE)

The ROE (OFB) lists the artificial obstacles of mainland French rivers, one
row per obstacle (`roe`, downloaded from the SANDRE WFS service).

```{r}
roe <- tar_read(roe)
basin <- tar_read(basin)
district_kept <- tar_read(params)$district_kept
```

```{r}
roe |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  count(LbEtOuvrage, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r}
roe |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  count(CdHautChutClObstEcoul, LbHautChutClObstEcoul)
```

## Large dams

The drop height is given twice: as a measured value
(`HautChutEtObstEcoul`) and as a class (`LbHautChutClObstEcoul`). The
measured value is missing for most obstacles, and holds obvious errors,
such as weirs of more than 100 m.

```{r}
class_bounds <- tibble(
  CdHautChutClObstEcoul = as.character(1:8),
  lower = c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 5, 10),
  upper = c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 5, 10, Inf)
)
roe_height <- roe |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      startsWith(CdTypeOuvrage, "1.1") ~ "dam",
      startsWith(CdTypeOuvrage, "1.2") ~ "weir",
      .default = "other"
    ),
    drop_height = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(HautChutEtObstEcoul))
  ) |>
  left_join(class_bounds, by = "CdHautChutClObstEcoul")

roe_height |>
  summarise(
    obstacles = n(),
    measured = mean(!is.na(drop_height)),
    class_known = mean(!is.na(lower)),
    .by = group
  )
```

Agreement between the measured value and the class, for obstacles with a
measured drop height >= 5 m or a class >= 5 m.

```{r}
roe_height |>
  filter(drop_height >= 5 | lower >= 5) |>
  mutate(
    agreement = case_when(
      is.na(drop_height) ~ "class only",
      is.na(lower) ~ "measured only",
      drop_height >= lower & drop_height < upper ~ "agree",
      .default = "disagree"
    )
  ) |>
  count(group, agreement) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = agreement, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
```

```{r}
roe_height |>
  filter(drop_height > 60) |>
  arrange(desc(drop_height)) |>
  select(
    name = NomPrincipalObstEcoul, type = LbTypeOuvrage, drop_height,
    class = LbHautChutClObstEcoul
  ) |>
  head(15)
```

Large dams are therefore selected on the class: existing obstacles of the
5-10 m or >= 10 m class, whatever their type (`large_dam`). The two
thresholds of 5 m and 10 m match class boundaries. Known large dams fall in
the >= 10 m class:

```{r}
large_dam <- tar_read(large_dam)

roe_height |>
  filter(grepl(
    "serre-pon|vouglans|bort les|sarrans|grangent|villerest|guerlédan$|rophémel|tuilières",
    NomPrincipalObstEcoul, ignore.case = TRUE
  )) |>
  select(
    name = NomPrincipalObstEcoul, state = LbEtOuvrage, drop_height,
    class = LbHautChutClObstEcoul
  )
```

```{r}
large_dam |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  count(
    threshold = paste(">=", drop_height_min, "m"),
    on_network = !is.na(node_id)
  )
```

AMOBIO network nodes include the ROE obstacles (`OE_ID`, the ROE code), so
large dams are placed on the network by their code, without snapping
(`obstacle_node_amobio`). The network was built with nodes at the ROE
obstacles: a large dam with a node lies at a median of a few metres from it.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 10

basin_kept <- basin |>
  filter(district %in% district_kept) |>
  sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(large_dam))
large_dam_kept <- large_dam |>
  sf::st_filter(basin_kept) |>
  mutate(threshold = factor(
    drop_height_min, levels = c(5, 10), labels = c("5-10 m", ">= 10 m")
  ))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = basin_kept, fill = "grey97", color = "grey40") +
  geom_sf(
    data = large_dam_kept |> arrange(drop_height_min),
    aes(color = threshold, shape = !is.na(node_id)),
    size = 1.2
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Drop height", values = c("#E69F00", "#B2182B")) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    name = "On the AMOBIO network", values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 4)
  ) +
  theme_void()
```

Large dams without a node: Strahler order of the nearest RHT reach, share
without a river name, and distance to the nearest network node.

```{r}
rht <- tar_read(rht)
network_node <- tar_read(river_network_full)$nodes |> sf::st_as_sf()

large_dam_rht <- large_dam |>
  sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(rht)) |>
  mutate(
    on_network = !is.na(node_id),
    strahler = rht$strahler[sf::st_nearest_feature(geom, rht)],
    no_river_name = is.na(river) | river == "",
    pond = grepl(
      "etang|étang|plan d|lac|retenue|réservoir|reservoir", name,
      ignore.case = TRUE
    )
  )
large_dam_rht |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  count(on_network, strahler) |>
  mutate(share = round(n / sum(n), 2), .by = on_network) |>
  select(-n) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = on_network, values_from = share, names_prefix = "on_network_")
```

```{r}
off_network <- large_dam |>
  filter(is.na(node_id)) |>
  sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(network_node))
off_network |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  left_join(
    large_dam_rht |> sf::st_drop_geometry() |> select(roe_code, no_river_name, pond),
    by = "roe_code"
  ) |>
  mutate(node_dist_m = as.numeric(sf::st_distance(
    off_network, network_node[sf::st_nearest_feature(off_network, network_node), ],
    by_element = TRUE
  ))) |>
  summarise(
    dams = n(),
    no_river_name = mean(no_river_name),
    pond_or_reservoir_name = mean(pond),
    median_node_dist_m = median(node_dist_m),
    .by = drop_height_min
  )
```

*To discuss: large dams off the network are mostly on Strahler 1 reaches,
without a river name, often pond or irrigation reservoir dams, a few
hundred metres from the network (streams not in AMOBIO). Large dams of the
"weir" type, obstacles with an undetermined class but a large measured drop
height (left out).*

## Dams along the river network

The network is oriented by the shortest-path tree from the river mouths. An
operation is upstream of a dam if the dam lies on its path to the mouth, and
downstream if it lies on the dam's path to the mouth (`operation_dam`, river
(ASPE) operations). The same is done between dams (`dam_dam`).

```{r}
operation_dam <- tar_read(operation_dam) |>
  left_join(
    tar_read(river_operation) |> distinct(operation_id, sandre_code),
    by = "operation_id"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    large_dam |> sf::st_drop_geometry() |> select(roe_code, drop_height_min),
    by = "roe_code"
  )
dam_dam <- tar_read(dam_dam)
river_ops <- tar_read(inland_operations_snapped) |>
  filter(survey == "river") |>
  left_join(
    tar_read(inland_distance_to_mouth) |> select(operation_id, dist_mouth_m),
    by = "operation_id"
  )

dam_below <- operation_dam |>
  filter(position == "upstream") |>
  summarise(
    dam_5 = n(),
    dam_10 = sum(drop_height_min == 10),
    .by = operation_id
  )
river_ops <- river_ops |>
  left_join(dam_below, by = "operation_id") |>
  mutate(across(c(dam_5, dam_10), \(x) coalesce(x, 0L)))

river_ops |>
  summarise(
    operations = n(),
    with_dam_5_below = mean(dam_5 > 0),
    with_dam_10_below = mean(dam_10 > 0)
  )
```

Number of large dams between each operation and the sea.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6

river_ops |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    c(dam_5, dam_10), names_to = "threshold", values_to = "dams"
  ) |>
  mutate(threshold = factor(
    threshold, levels = c("dam_5", "dam_10"), labels = c(">= 5 m", ">= 10 m")
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(longitude, latitude, color = pmin(dams, 5))) +
  geom_sf(
    data = sf::st_transform(basin_kept, 4326), fill = "grey97",
    color = "grey40", inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 0.6) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Large dams\ndownstream", labels = c(0:4, "5+")) +
  facet_wrap(~threshold) +
  theme_void()
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5

ggplot(river_ops, aes(dist_mouth_m / 1000, dam_5)) +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.2, size = 0.5, alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~district) +
  labs(x = "Distance to the mouth (km)", y = "Large dams (>= 5 m) downstream")
```

## Case-study areas

Before a model over all operations, the impact of dams is looked for around
a few dams, first on migratory species: one large dam near the sea and one
in the mountains, with ASPE sites both upstream and downstream. For each
large dam: distinct sites within 50 km of river upstream and downstream,
large dams below it, and its distance to the mouth (from the operations
located relative to it).

```{r}
window_m <- 50000

dam_dist_mouth <- operation_dam |>
  inner_join(river_ops |> select(operation_id, dist_mouth_m), by = "operation_id") |>
  mutate(dam_dist_mouth_m = if_else(
    position == "upstream", dist_mouth_m - river_dist_m, dist_mouth_m + river_dist_m
  )) |>
  summarise(dam_dist_mouth_km = median(dam_dist_mouth_m) / 1000, .by = roe_code)

dam_site <- operation_dam |>
  filter(river_dist_m <= window_m) |>
  summarise(sites = n_distinct(sandre_code), .by = c(roe_code, position)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = position, values_from = sites, names_prefix = "sites_",
    values_fill = 0
  )

candidate <- large_dam |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  inner_join(dam_site, by = "roe_code") |>
  left_join(dam_dist_mouth, by = "roe_code") |>
  left_join(
    dam_dam |> filter(position == "upstream") |>
      count(roe_code = operation_id, name = "dams_below"),
    by = "roe_code"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    dams_below = coalesce(dams_below, 0L),
    min_sites = pmin(sites_upstream, sites_downstream)
  ) |>
  filter(min_sites >= 2) |>
  select(
    roe_code, name, river, drop_height_min, drop_height, altitude,
    dam_dist_mouth_km, dams_below, sites_upstream, sites_downstream
  )
```

First large dam from the sea (no large dam below):

```{r}
candidate |>
  filter(dams_below == 0) |>
  arrange(dam_dist_mouth_km) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

Mountain dams (altitude > 400 m):

```{r}
candidate |>
  filter(altitude > 400) |>
  arrange(desc(altitude)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

Migratory species sampled in the river (ASPE) operations. Shads are not
caught by electrofishing, and sea trout are not told apart from brown
trout (*Salmo trutta*).

```{r}
migratory <- c(
  "Anguilla anguilla", "Salmo salar", "Petromyzon marinus",
  "Lampetra fluviatilis", "Platichthys flesus", "Chelon ramada", "Chelon auratus"
)
tar_read(size_year_filtered) |>
  filter(survey == "river", species_valid %in% migratory) |>
  count(operation_id, species_valid) |>
  summarise(
    operations = n(),
    median_individuals = median(n),
    .by = species_valid
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(operations))
```

*To discuss: few sites on each side (2-7 within 50 km); upstream sites also
differ along the continuum (PC1).*

## Case studies: Mervent and Tuilières

Mervent (Vendée) is the first large dam from the sea on the Vendée (24 m
drop, 49 km from the mouth). Tuilières (Dordogne) is the first large dam on
the Dordogne (5-10 m class, 148 km from the mouth). All ASPE sites on the
same flow path within 100 km, with the signed river distance to the dam
(negative: downstream).

```{r}
focus_dam <- c(Mervent = "ROE39720", Tuilieres = "ROE66029")
river_effort <- tar_read(river_effort)

focus_operation <- operation_dam |>
  filter(roe_code %in% focus_dam, river_dist_m <= 100000) |>
  mutate(
    dam = names(focus_dam)[match(roe_code, focus_dam)],
    signed_km = if_else(position == "upstream", 1, -1) * river_dist_m / 1000
  ) |>
  left_join(
    tar_read(river_operation) |> distinct(operation_id, year),
    by = "operation_id"
  ) |>
  left_join(river_effort, by = "operation_id")

focus_operation |>
  summarise(
    km = round(median(signed_km), 1),
    operations = n(),
    with_individuals = sum(has_individuals),
    years = paste(range(year), collapse = "-"),
    protocol = paste(unique(protocol), collapse = ", "),
    .by = c(dam, sandre_code)
  ) |>
  arrange(dam, km) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

### All species upstream and downstream

Occurrence of each species (share of operations where it is caught),
downstream and upstream of each dam, for the operations with individual fish
records. The effect of the dam is summarised by the difference in occurrence
(upstream minus downstream; negative: less frequent upstream).

```{r}
focus_presence <- tar_read(river_size) |>
  mutate(operation_id = as.character(operation_id)) |>
  semi_join(focus_operation, by = "operation_id") |>
  distinct(operation_id, species_valid)

focus_species <- focus_operation |>
  filter(has_individuals) |>
  tidyr::crossing(species_valid = unique(focus_presence$species_valid)) |>
  left_join(
    focus_presence |> mutate(present = TRUE),
    by = c("operation_id", "species_valid")
  ) |>
  summarise(
    occurrence = mean(coalesce(present, FALSE)),
    .by = c(dam, species_valid, position)
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = position, values_from = occurrence, names_prefix = "occurrence_"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    difference = occurrence_upstream - occurrence_downstream,
    migratory = species_valid %in% migratory
  )

focus_operation |>
  filter(has_individuals) |>
  count(dam, position, name = "operations")
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 9

difference_plot <- function(dam_name) {
  focus_species |>
    filter(dam == dam_name) |>
    mutate(species_valid = reorder(species_valid, difference)) |>
    ggplot(aes(difference, species_valid, color = migratory)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = difference, yend = species_valid)) +
    geom_point() +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey40", `TRUE` = "#B2182B")) +
    labs(
      title = dam_name, x = "Occurrence upstream - occurrence downstream",
      y = NULL, color = "Migratory"
    ) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"))
}
patchwork::wrap_plots(lapply(names(focus_dam), difference_plot), guides = "collect")
```

**Results:** eel is less frequent upstream of both dams (Mervent: 1.00
downstream vs 0.62 upstream; Tuilières: 1.00 vs 0.33), flounder and thinlip
mullet are absent above Mervent, golden grey mullet and sea lamprey above
Tuilières. The other species with the largest differences are lowland
species downstream (white bream, black bullhead, largemouth bass, wels
catfish) and small-stream species upstream (stone loach, minnow, gudgeon,
bullhead).

Position of the operations along the continuum (D11 PC1, operations matched
to the RHT).

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3

continuum_operation <- tar_read(continuum_operation)

focus_operation |>
  filter(has_individuals) |>
  inner_join(continuum_operation |> select(operation_id, PC1), by = "operation_id") |>
  ggplot(aes(PC1, dam, color = position)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7, position = position_jitter(height = 0.1, seed = 1)) +
  labs(y = NULL, color = NULL)
```

**Results:** downstream sites sit at PC1 of about 4.2-4.8 (large lowland
rivers), upstream sites at -1.5 to 0.5 (small streams): the contrast mixes
the dam with the upstream-downstream change in community.

*To discuss: downstream sites fished by points, upstream completely; 12
(Mervent) and 6 (Tuilières) operations with fish records.*

### Operations without individual fish records

The individual fish file (`output_individual_fish.rda`) has records for
less than half of the river operations, none flagged as without fish.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.5

river_effort |>
  left_join(
    tar_read(river_operation) |> distinct(operation_id, year),
    by = "operation_id"
  ) |>
  filter(year >= 2005) |>
  count(year, has_individuals) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, n, fill = has_individuals)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(`TRUE` = "grey30", `FALSE` = "grey75"),
    labels = c(`TRUE` = "with records", `FALSE` = "without records")
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "River operations", fill = NULL)
```

**Results:** 12,419 of 27,889 river operations have individual fish
records; about 45% per year until 2017, 6% in 2018, 75% in 2019-2020, 7% in
2021 and none in 2022.

*To discuss: origin of the missing operations (ASPE extract), effect on
D10/D11 food webs.*

## Impact on species

All large dams (>= 5 m) are used from here on.

### Visits and dam accumulation

All river (ASPE) sites with a PC1 score and individual fish records. Visits
are grouped in four periods (2005-2009, 2010-2013, 2014-2017, 2018-2021),
and the latest visit of each site in each period is kept (site x period).
Sampling effort is the fishing protocol and the fished surface
(`computed_surface`; for the partial protocol by points, 12.5 m² per
point). Dam accumulation is the number of large dams between the site and
the sea (`dams`), or their cumulative drop height (`cum_height`). The drop
height of a dam is its measured value when it agrees with its class, else
the class lower bound (5 or 10 m).

```{r}
presence <- tar_read(size_year_filtered) |>
  filter(survey == "river") |>
  distinct(operation_id, species_valid)

dam_height <- large_dam |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(
    height = if_else(
      !is.na(drop_height) & drop_height >= drop_height_min &
        (drop_height_min == 10 | drop_height < 10),
      drop_height, drop_height_min
    )
  ) |>
  select(roe_code, height)

dam_accumulation <- operation_dam |>
  filter(position == "upstream") |>
  left_join(dam_height, by = "roe_code") |>
  summarise(dams = n(), cum_height = sum(height), .by = operation_id)

visit <- continuum_operation |>
  select(operation_id, longitude, latitude, district, PC1, PC2, log_altitude) |>
  filter(!is.na(log_altitude)) |>
  semi_join(presence, by = "operation_id") |>
  inner_join(
    tar_read(river_operation) |> distinct(operation_id, sandre_code, date, year),
    by = "operation_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(period = cut(
    year, c(2004, 2009, 2013, 2017, 2021),
    labels = c("2005-2009", "2010-2013", "2014-2017", "2018-2021")
  )) |>
  slice_max(date, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE, by = c(sandre_code, period)) |>
  left_join(river_effort |> select(operation_id, protocol, surface), by = "operation_id") |>
  filter(!is.na(surface)) |>
  left_join(
    tar_read(inland_operations_rht) |>
      sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
      select(operation_id, altitude, july_temperature = tjuil_moy),
    by = "operation_id"
  ) |>
  left_join(dam_accumulation, by = "operation_id") |>
  mutate(
    dams = coalesce(dams, 0L),
    cum_height = coalesce(cum_height, 0),
    sandre_code = factor(sandre_code)
  )
c(visits = nrow(visit), sites = n_distinct(visit$sandre_code))
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4

visit_site <- distinct(visit, sandre_code, .keep_all = TRUE)
patchwork::wrap_plots(
  ggplot(visit_site, aes(PC1, pmin(dams, 6))) +
    geom_jitter(height = 0.15, size = 0.5, alpha = 0.4) +
    labs(y = "Large dams downstream (6 = 6+)"),
  ggplot(visit_site, aes(altitude, pmin(dams, 6))) +
    geom_jitter(height = 0.15, size = 0.5, alpha = 0.4) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    labs(x = "Altitude (m, RHT)", y = NULL)
)
```

**Results:**

### Choice of the controls

D11 PCA loadings of the continuum variables on PC1 and PC2.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.5

tar_read(continuum_pca)$rotation[, 1:2] |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "variable") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(PC1, PC2), names_to = "axis", values_to = "loading") |>
  ggplot(aes(loading, variable)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~axis) +
  labs(x = "Loading", y = NULL)
```

**Results:** PC1 is river size (width, Strahler order, distance to source);
altitude loads mainly on PC2 (0.62), with the distance to the mouth (0.69).
Sites with dams below are upland sites (Spearman correlation of
log(1 + dams) with log altitude: 0.61, with PC1: -0.31),
so PC1 alone leaves altitude as a confounder.

Binomial GLMMs of presence (`glmmTMB`) for four illustrative species (eel,
migratory; brown trout and chub, native residents; pumpkinseed,
non-native), with log(1 + dams), alternative controls (quadratic), the district,
the sampling effort (protocol and log fished surface) and random effects of
the site and the period.

```{r}
species_kept <- c("Anguilla anguilla", "Salmo trutta", "Squalius cephalus", "Lepomis gibbosus")

control_term <- c(
  PC1 = "PC1 + I(PC1^2)",
  PC1_PC2 = "PC1 + I(PC1^2) + PC2 + I(PC2^2)",
  PC1_altitude = "PC1 + I(PC1^2) + log_altitude + I(log_altitude^2)"
)
effort_term <- "district + protocol + log(surface) + (1 | sandre_code) + (1 | period)"
# BFGS converges when a random effect variance is near zero (migratory
# richness), where the default optimiser leaves a non-positive-definite
# Hessian.
glmm_control <- glmmTMB::glmmTMBControl(optimizer = optim, optArgs = list(method = "BFGS"))

fit_presence <- function(species, score, control) {
  data <- visit |>
    mutate(
      present = operation_id %in% presence$operation_id[presence$species_valid == species],
      accumulation = log1p(.data[[score]])
    )
  model <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
    as.formula(paste("present ~ accumulation +", control, "+", effort_term)),
    family = binomial, data = data, control = glmm_control
  )
  coefficient <- summary(model)$coefficients$cond["accumulation", ]
  tibble(
    species = species, presences = sum(data$present),
    estimate = coefficient[["Estimate"]], se = coefficient[["Std. Error"]],
    aic = AIC(model)
  )
}

control_comparison <- tidyr::expand_grid(species = species_kept, control = names(control_term)) |>
  mutate(fit = parallel::mcmapply(
    \(x, y) fit_presence(x, "dams", control_term[[y]]), species, control,
    SIMPLIFY = FALSE, mc.cores = 8
  )) |>
  select(-species) |>
  tidyr::unnest(fit) |>
  mutate(control = factor(control, levels = names(control_term)))
```

```{r}

#| fig-height: 4.5

  summarise(delta_aic = sum(aic), .by = control) |>
  mutate(delta_aic = delta_aic - min(delta_aic))

patchwork::wrap_plots(
  ggplot(control_summary, aes(delta_aic, control)) +
    geom_col() +
    labs(x = "Summed AIC - best", y = NULL),
  control_comparison |>
    ggplot(aes(estimate, control)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = estimate - 2 * se, xmax = estimate + 2 * se), size = 0.2) +
    facet_wrap(~species, nrow = 1) +
    labs(x = "Effect of log(1 + dams)", y = NULL) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "italic")),
  widths = c(1, 4)
)
```

**Results:**

PC1 and PC2 are kept as controls for the species and richness models.

*To discuss: PC2 contains the distance to the mouth, along which the number
of dams downstream grows by construction.*

### Presence models

Binomial GLMM per species: presence ~ log(1 + dams) + PC1 + PC2
(quadratic) + district + protocol + log(surface) + (1 | site) + (1 |
period). Species are grouped as migratory (sea-dependent: eel, salmon,
lampreys, flounder, mullets), non-native (FishBase) and native resident.
FishBase's diadromous flag is not used: it includes perch, sticklebacks,
rainbow and brown trout.

```{r}
species_group <- presence |>
  distinct(species = species_valid) |>
  left_join(tar_read(species_traits) |> select(species, is_native), by = "species") |>
  mutate(group = case_when(
    species %in% migratory ~ "migratory",
    !is_native ~ "non-native",
    .default = "native resident"
  ))

presence_effect <- control_comparison |>
  filter(control == "PC1_PC2") |>
  select(-control) |>
  left_join(species_group |> select(species, group), by = "species")
```

```{r}

#| fig-height: 3

group_color <- c(
  migratory = "#B2182B", `non-native` = "#E69F00", `native resident` = "grey40"
)
presence_effect |>
  mutate(species = reorder(species, -estimate)) |>
  ggplot(aes(estimate, species, color = group)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = estimate - 2 * se, xmax = estimate + 2 * se), size = 0.3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = group_color) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-3, 2)) +
  labs(x = "Effect of log(1 + large dams downstream)", y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"))
```

### Accumulation score: number of dams or cumulative drop height

Same models with log(1 + cumulative drop height) instead of log(1 + number
of dams). Each point is a species: z-values of the two scores, coloured by
the AIC difference (negative: drop height fits better).

```{r}

score_comparison <- species_kept |>
  parallel::mclapply(
    fit_presence, score = "cum_height", control = control_term[["PC1_PC2"]], mc.cores = 8
  ) |>
  bind_rows() |>

    presence_effect |> select(species, aic_dams = aic, estimate_dams = estimate, se_dams = se),
    by = "species"

  mutate(
    z_dams = estimate_dams / se_dams,
    z_height = estimate / se,
```

### Accumulation curves

Predicted probability of presence against the number of large dams
downstream (as a factor: 0, 1, 2, 3+), other covariates at their median
(district Loire, complete protocol, random effects at zero).

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4

accumulation_curve <- function(species) {
  data <- visit |>
    mutate(
      present = operation_id %in% presence$operation_id[presence$species_valid == species],
      dams = factor(pmin(dams, 3), labels = c("0", "1", "2", "3+"))
    )
  model <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
    as.formula(paste("present ~ dams +", control_term[["PC1_PC2"]], "+", effort_term)),
    family = binomial, data = data, control = glmm_control
  )
  new_data <- tibble(
    dams = factor(levels(data$dams), levels = levels(data$dams)),
    PC1 = median(data$PC1), PC2 = median(data$PC2),
    district = "Loire", protocol = "complete", surface = median(data$surface),
    sandre_code = NA, period = NA
  )
  prediction <- predict(model, new_data, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE, re.form = NA)
  new_data |>
    mutate(
      species = species,
      probability = plogis(prediction$fit),
      lower = plogis(prediction$fit - 2 * prediction$se.fit),
      upper = plogis(prediction$fit + 2 * prediction$se.fit)
    )
}

accumulation <- species_kept |>
  lapply(accumulation_curve) |>
  bind_rows()

ggplot(accumulation, aes(dams, probability)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper)) +
  facet_wrap(~species, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Large dams downstream", y = "Probability of presence")
```

**Results:**

### Local richness per species group

Poisson GLMMs of the number of species per visit, in total and per group,
with the same covariates and random effects. All species are counted, not
only those in >= 30 sites. Effect shown as the expected richness with one
large dam downstream relative to none.

```{r}

#| fig-height: 3.5

  semi_join(visit, by = "operation_id") |>

  count(operation_id, group) |>

  mutate(total = migratory + `non-native` + `native resident`)
visit_richness <- visit |> left_join(richness, by = "operation_id")

richness_effect <- c("total", "native resident", "migratory", "non-native") |>
  lapply(function(response) {
    model <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
      as.formula(paste0(
        "`", response, "` ~ log1p(dams) + ", control_term[["PC1_PC2"]], " + ", effort_term
      )),
      family = poisson, data = visit_richness, control = glmm_control
    )
    coefficient <- summary(model)$coefficients$cond["log1p(dams)", ]
    tibble(
      richness = response,
      estimate = coefficient[["Estimate"]], se = coefficient[["Std. Error"]]
    )
  }) |>

richness_effect |>
  mutate(richness = factor(richness, levels = rev(richness))) |>
  ggplot(aes(exp(estimate * log(2)), richness)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
```

**Results:**

### Richness along the distance to the nearest large dam

Richness around a dam: the river distance from the site to its nearest
large dam downstream (the site is upstream of the dam, on the reservoir
side; positive distance) and to its nearest large dam upstream (the site is
below the dam; negative distance). Both enter the same GLMM, each as a step
(the site has a large dam on that side) plus a natural spline of
log(1 + distance) (3 degrees of freedom), so that each curve is the
richness relative to sites without a large dam on that side. The other
large dams downstream (all but the nearest one), the controls, the effort,
and the site and period random effects are in the model. Curves are drawn
between the 5th and 95th percentiles of the observed distances.

```{r}
nearest_dam <- operation_dam |>
  summarise(distance_km = min(river_dist_m) / 1000, .by = c(operation_id, position)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = position, values_from = distance_km)

visit_distance <- visit_richness |>
  left_join(
    nearest_dam |> select(operation_id, above_km = upstream, below_km = downstream),
    by = "operation_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    # above_km: the site is above its nearest dam downstream; below_km: the
    # site is below its nearest dam upstream.
    has_above = as.numeric(!is.na(above_km)),
    has_below = as.numeric(!is.na(below_km)),
    other_dams = dams - has_above
  ) |>
  rename(non_native = `non-native`, native_resident = `native resident`)

# Natural spline basis of log(1 + distance), knots from the sites with a
# dam on that side, zero for the sites without.
distance_basis <- lapply(c(above = "above_km", below = "below_km"), function(x) {
  log_km <- log1p(visit_distance[[x]])
  knots <- quantile(log_km, c(1 / 3, 2 / 3), na.rm = TRUE)
  boundary <- c(0, max(log_km, na.rm = TRUE))
  \(km) splines::ns(log1p(km), knots = knots, Boundary.knots = boundary)
})
for (x in c("above", "below")) {
  basis <- distance_basis[[x]](coalesce(visit_distance[[paste0(x, "_km")]], 0)) *
    visit_distance[[paste0("has_", x)]]
  visit_distance[paste0(x, "_", 1:3)] <- as.data.frame(unclass(basis))
}

distance_formula <- paste(
  "~ has_above + above_1 + above_2 + above_3 + has_below + below_1 + below_2 + below_3 +",
  "log1p(other_dams) +", control_term[["PC1_PC2"]], "+", effort_term
)

distance_curve <- function(response, family) {
  model <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
    as.formula(paste(response, distance_formula)),
    family = family, data = visit_distance, control = glmm_control
  )
  lapply(c("above", "below"), function(x) {
    term <- c(paste0("has_", x), paste0(x, "_", 1:3))
    km <- quantile(visit_distance[[paste0(x, "_km")]], c(0.05, 0.95), na.rm = TRUE)
    km <- seq(km[1], km[2], length.out = 100)
    design <- cbind(1, unclass(distance_basis[[x]](km)))
    covariance <- vcov(model)$cond[term, term]
    tibble(
      response = response,
      distance_km = if (x == "above") km else -km,
      effect = as.vector(design %*% glmmTMB::fixef(model)$cond[term]),
      se = sqrt(rowSums((design %*% covariance) * design))
    )
  }) |>
    bind_rows()
}

distance_species <- species_kept
for (species in distance_species) {
  visit_distance[[gsub(" ", "_", species)]] <- as.numeric(
    visit_distance$operation_id %in% presence$operation_id[presence$species_valid == species]
  )
}
distance_effect <- c(
  total = "poisson", migratory = "poisson", non_native = "poisson",
  native_resident = "poisson",
  setNames(rep("binomial", length(distance_species)), gsub(" ", "_", distance_species))
) |>
  (\(x) parallel::mcmapply(
    \(family, response) distance_curve(response, get(family)), x, names(x),
    SIMPLIFY = FALSE, mc.cores = 8
  ))() |>
  bind_rows()
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6

distance_rug <- bind_rows(
  visit_distance |> filter(has_above == 1) |> transmute(distance_km = above_km),
  visit_distance |> filter(has_below == 1) |> transmute(distance_km = -below_km)
)
distance_effect |>
  mutate(response = factor(response, levels = unique(response))) |>
  ggplot(aes(distance_km, exp(effect))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey50") +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = exp(effect - 2 * se), ymax = exp(effect + 2 * se), group = distance_km > 0),
    fill = "grey80"
  ) +
  geom_line(aes(group = distance_km > 0), color = "#B2182B") +
  geom_rug(data = distance_rug, aes(distance_km), inherit.aes = FALSE, alpha = 0.1) +
  facet_wrap(~response, nrow = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(transform = scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 1), breaks = c(-100, -20, -5, 0, 5, 20, 100)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "River distance to the nearest large dam (km; < 0: below the dam, > 0: above the dam)",
    y = "Relative to no dam on that side"
  )
```

Top row: richness ratio; bottom row: odds ratio of presence.

**Results:**

## Impact on diversity

### Beta, gamma and alpha diversity against dams

Diversity is computed in hydrographic sectors (BD Carthage, SANDRE; groups
of sub-catchments, median 2,400 km²) x periods (as above, latest visit of
each site per period). Sector x periods with >= 10 sites are kept. In each,
10 sites are drawn 100 times, and averaged over the draws: beta, the
multi-site Sørensen dissimilarity of the 10 sites (Baselga 2010); gamma,
their number of species; alpha, their mean richness.

Two dam measures: the dam density (number of large dams, on or off the
AMOBIO network, per 100 km of RHT river in the sector, log(1 + x)) and the
share of the sites with at least one large dam downstream. Gaussian INLA
models of each response on one dam measure, with the mean and standard
deviation of PC1 and PC2 of the sites (position along the continuum and
environmental heterogeneity), the mean log fished surface of the sites
(effort), a BYM2 spatial effect on the adjacency of the sectors and a
period random effect (iid). All covariates are standardised: effects are
per standard deviation of the dam measure.

```{r}
species_list <- split(presence$species_valid, presence$operation_id)
basin_l93 <- sf::st_transform(basin_kept, sf::st_crs(rht))
visit_sf <- visit |>
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(rht))

sector <- tar_read(hydro_sector) |>
  sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(rht)) |>
  sf::st_set_geometry("geometry") |>
  select(sector) |>
  sf::st_filter(basin_l93)

sector_dam <- rht |>
  select(id_drain) |>
  sf::st_intersection(sector) |>
  mutate(length_km = as.numeric(sf::st_length(geometry)) / 1000) |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  summarise(river_km = sum(length_km), .by = sector) |>
  left_join(
    large_dam |>
      sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(rht)) |>
      select(roe_code) |>
      sf::st_join(sector) |>
      sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
      filter(!is.na(sector)) |>
      count(sector, name = "n_dams"),
    by = "sector"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    n_dams = coalesce(n_dams, 0L),
    dam_density = 100 * n_dams / river_km
  )

# Multi-site Sørensen dissimilarity (Baselga 2010) of a site x species
# incidence matrix.
multi_site_sorensen <- function(incidence) {
  pair <- combn(nrow(incidence), 2)
  b_ij <- rowSums(incidence[pair[1, ], , drop = FALSE] & !incidence[pair[2, ], , drop = FALSE])
  b_ji <- rowSums(incidence[pair[2, ], , drop = FALSE] & !incidence[pair[1, ], , drop = FALSE])
  a <- sum(incidence) - ncol(incidence)
  (sum(pmin(b_ij, b_ji)) + sum(pmax(b_ij, b_ji))) /
    (2 * a + sum(pmin(b_ij, b_ji)) + sum(pmax(b_ij, b_ji)))
}

set.seed(1)
sector_diversity <- visit_sf |>
  sf::st_join(sector) |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(!is.na(sector)) |>
  filter(n() >= 10, .by = c(sector, period)) |>
  group_by(sector, period) |>
  group_modify(function(x, key) {
    draws <- replicate(100, {
      operation_id <- sample(x$operation_id, 10)
      species <- unique(unlist(species_list[operation_id]))
      incidence <- t(vapply(
        species_list[operation_id], \(s) species %in% s, logical(length(species))
      ))
      c(
        beta = multi_site_sorensen(incidence),
        gamma = length(species), alpha = mean(rowSums(incidence))
      )
    })
    as_tibble(as.list(rowMeans(draws))) |>
      mutate(
        sites = nrow(x),
        PC1 = mean(x$PC1), PC2 = mean(x$PC2),
        sd_PC1 = sd(x$PC1), sd_PC2 = sd(x$PC2),
        log_surface = mean(log(x$surface)),
        dammed_sites = mean(x$dams > 0)
      )
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(sector_dam, by = "sector")
count(sector_diversity, period)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5

sector_map <- sector |>
  inner_join(
    sector_diversity |> summarise(beta = mean(beta), dam_density = first(dam_density), .by = sector),
    by = "sector"
  )
patchwork::wrap_plots(
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = basin_l93, fill = "grey97", color = "grey40") +
    geom_sf(data = sector_map, aes(fill = dam_density), color = "white") +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Large dams\nper 100 km") +
    theme_void(),
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = basin_l93, fill = "grey97", color = "grey40") +
    geom_sf(data = sector_map, aes(fill = beta), color = "white") +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Beta, mean\nover periods", option = "magma") +
    theme_void()
)
```

```{r}
diversity_response <- c("beta", "gamma", "alpha")
dam_measure <- c("dam_density", "dammed_sites")
diversity_control <- c("PC1", "PC2", "sd_PC1", "sd_PC2", "log_surface")

diversity_data <- sector_diversity |>
  mutate(
    dam_density = log1p(dam_density),
    across(c(all_of(dam_measure), all_of(diversity_control)), \(x) as.numeric(scale(x))),
    index = match(sector, unique(sector))
  )
sector_kept <- sector[match(unique(diversity_data$sector), sector$sector), ]
adjacency <- sf::st_relate(sector_kept, sector_kept, pattern = "F***T****", sparse = FALSE) * 1

fit_diversity <- function(response, dam) {
  data <- diversity_data |> mutate(dam = .data[[dam]])
  model <- INLA::inla(
    as.formula(paste(
      response, "~ dam +", paste(diversity_control, collapse = " + "), "+",
      "f(index, model = 'bym2', graph = adjacency, scale.model = TRUE) +",
      "f(period, model = 'iid')"
    )),
    data = data, family = "gaussian", num.threads = 1,
    control.compute = list(config = FALSE)
  )
  effect <- model$summary.fixed["dam", ]
  fitted <- model$summary.fitted.values$mean
  gc()
  tibble(
    response = response, dam = dam,
    mean = effect$mean, lower = effect$`0.025quant`, upper = effect$`0.975quant`,
    point = list(tibble(
      x = data$dam,
      period = data$period,
      fitted = fitted,
      residual = data[[response]] - fitted,
      # Response minus the intercept and the controls (random effects left in).
      partial = data[[response]] - model$summary.fixed$mean[1] -
        as.vector(as.matrix(data[diversity_control]) %*%
          model$summary.fixed[diversity_control, "mean"])
    ))
  )
}

diversity_effect <- tidyr::expand_grid(response = diversity_response, dam = dam_measure) |>
  purrr::pmap(fit_diversity) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(response = factor(response, levels = diversity_response))
```

Effect of one standard deviation of the dam measure on each response
(posterior mean and 95% credible interval).

```{r}
diversity_effect |>

  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~response, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = c(
    dam_density = "Dam density", dammed_sites = "Share of sites\nwith a dam below"
  )) +
  labs(x = "Effect (per SD of the dam measure)", y = NULL)
```

```{r}
patchwork::wrap_plots(
```
